note:
Commit-validity conformance vectors for spec 014's rules 1-5 (§"Membership change").
Commit validity is where two implementations reaching different verdicts on the same bytes split
a group irreparably, so each vector pins the whole input as data and the verdict as one of
"apply" (014's "valid under this profile"), "wait", or "invalid".

Bytes are unpadded base64url: `authenticatedData` is the PNCommitBinding of the commit's
`authenticated_data`, `credential` is a leaf's PNCredential, `signaturePublicKey` is a raw
32-byte Ed25519 key. `keyRef` is that key's spec-005 KeyRef, restated so evidence `leaves`
entries can be lined up by eye; it is derivable from `signaturePublicKey` and is checked
rather than trusted. Every evidence entry's `digest` is the spec-001/003 digest of its
`record`, and is the entry the binding names.

`evidence[].verified` is whether this member has resolved that record's OWN signature (owner
mode against the actor's key log, delegated mode against the presented chain). It is an input,
not a conclusion: resolution needs a network and commit validity must not, so the evaluator
takes the answer and treats held-but-unverified exactly like not-held — a wait.

`expected.reason` is the reference implementation's label. Two implementations MUST agree on
the VERDICT; the reason string is diagnostic and is not part of the wire contract.

Not represented here, deliberately: expiry, revocation status, and issuer key-state
resolution. Spec 014 excludes all three from commit validity — they are wall-clock- and
registry-dependent, so making them validity conditions would let two honest members split the
group. They survive as client-surfaced warnings and as grounds to author `device-remove`.

vectors.name: add — the creator adds a participant
vectors.comment: The baseline: one Add proposal, covered by one `add` record naming exactly the participant it brings in, at the epoch the commit extends, authored by the conversation's creator while the creator holds a leaf.

vectors.name: add — two participants under one record
vectors.comment: Set equality is per record, not per proposal: one record may cover several Adds as long as the participants those Adds bring in are exactly its `members`.

vectors.name: remove — the creator removes a participant
vectors.comment: Every leaf bob holds in the pre-commit tree is removed, so the complete-removal check passes and 'bob left' is true cryptographically as well as on screen.

vectors.name: remove — a self-authorized departure, committed by another member
vectors.comment: `members == [actor]` is self-authorizing, which is what lets anyone commit a departure — MLS forbids committing your own Remove, so a departure nobody else could commit would never land.

vectors.name: device-add — a member adds a second device
vectors.comment: A participant governs their own device set. The actor already holds a leaf in the tree the commit extends, so this is not a way *in*.

vectors.name: device-remove — a member retires one of two devices
vectors.comment: The actor keeps a leaf, so the device path cannot be used for the self-expulsion the `conversation/self-remove` ability exists to gate.

vectors.name: founding commit — initial members, empty binding
vectors.comment: The Conversation record is the coverage, at epoch 0: no `add` records are minted for bytes that already say exactly this, and the binding is the empty list. Every added leaf's credential subject must be one of the record's `participants`.

vectors.name: PCS commit — an update path touching no membership, empty binding
vectors.comment: Rule 5: valid from any leaf with an empty binding. The path leaf keeps its signature key and its credential subject, which is what credential refresh means under rule 4.

vectors.name: wait — the binding names a record this member does not hold
vectors.comment: No member can distinguish 'this names nothing' from 'this has not reached me yet', so an unheld digest is a wait. Waiting is safe because it is uniform: everyone lacking the record stalls, nobody diverges, and the stall clears monotonically once any member re-delivers it.

vectors.name: wait — the record is held but its own signature has not resolved
vectors.comment: Held-but-unverified is a wait on exactly the same footing as missing. Failing open would apply an authorization nobody checked; failing closed would split the group on a key-log cache miss. Key logs are monotone, so the stall converges.

vectors.name: add — authored by a member who is not the creator
vectors.comment: Add authority is creator-only; no member-adds and no succession in v1.

vectors.name: add — the creator has left the group
vectors.comment: Add authority ends when the creator leaves: a creator-less conversation is closed to new participants, while removals, device changes and messaging continue.

vectors.name: remove — authored by neither the creator nor the participant removed
vectors.comment: The only two removal authorities are the creator and the subject themselves.

vectors.name: device-add — authored by a participant holding no leaf in the group
vectors.comment: Without the 'actor already holds a leaf' clause a device-add is an unbounded membership bypass: anyone — including a participant who left, or was never a member — could author one for their own device and have any member commit it, defeating creator-only add authority.

vectors.name: device-remove — one named leaf's credential does not name the actor
vectors.comment: The ghost leaf's credential does not decode, so it contributes no participant to the exact-set check and reaches rule 2's per-leaf subject clause. A leaf whose credential names a *different* participant is caught one check earlier, by set equality — this is the shape that makes the subject clause load-bearing rather than redundant.

vectors.name: device-remove — taking the actor's last leaf
vectors.comment: Full departure is a `remove`, which a delegated signer may author for its own subject only with `conversation/self-remove`. A `device-remove` needs no more than the everyday `msg` umbrella and names public key refs, so without this rule the umbrella would keep unilateral self-expulsion authority by the device path.

vectors.name: device-remove — two records in one commit that jointly take the actor's last leaf
vectors.comment: The retained-leaf test is measured against every Remove the commit carries, not the ones a single record covers. Read per record, each of these two retains what the other takes and both pass — which is exactly the split an attacker would use.

vectors.name: exact participant set — a record covering a participant it does not name
vectors.comment: Set equality, never containment: containment would let a committer smuggle an extra participant in alongside a legitimate record.

vectors.name: complete removal — one of the removed participant's leaves stays in the tree
vectors.comment: A partial removal renders as 'bob left' at every client while one of bob's leaves — a stolen or ghost device, chosen by whoever authored the record — keeps decrypting.

vectors.name: uncovered Add — a second added leaf no named record covers
vectors.comment: The covered Add is legitimate; the second one rides along on it. Every Add and Remove must be covered by a named record, which is what makes 'an uncovered leaf cannot enter the group' true.

vectors.name: uncovered Remove — a second removed leaf no named record covers
vectors.comment: The mirror of the uncovered Add: an unauthorized eviction riding a legitimate one.

vectors.name: over-full binding — a named record covering no proposal in this commit
vectors.comment: Minimality runs both ways. Without the unused-entry rule the binding is a covert channel in cleartext on every commit — attacker-chosen bytes in a field 'fully specified shape' would happily admit.

vectors.name: non-empty binding on a commit that changes no membership
vectors.comment: The covert-channel case in its purest form: a PCS commit with a binding. The digest names a real record, and the commit still must not carry it.

vectors.name: binding — `authenticated_data` that is not a well-formed PNCommitBinding
vectors.comment: Trailing bytes after the length-prefixed body. The binding must have exactly one byte-form, so the codec fails closed on trailing bytes, non-minimal lengths, unsorted entries and duplicates alike.

vectors.name: epoch — an old `add` re-cited at a later epoch
vectors.comment: Without the one-shot an authorization is replayable forever: an old `add` could be re-cited to force a departed participant back in. Epoch *equality*, never a lower bound — a bound leaves the rejoin-then-replay window open.

vectors.name: epoch — a self-`remove` re-cited after the participant rejoined
vectors.comment: bob authorized their own departure at epoch 5 and was later re-added. Re-citing that record at epoch 9 would make a member's own past departure a permanent eviction warrant in anyone's hands.

vectors.name: cross-conversation replay — a record authorizing a change in another conversation
vectors.comment: Without the conversation check a record travels between groups: a departure from one conversation would evict its author from every other, and a `device-add` harvested anywhere would insert that leaf here.

vectors.name: update path — rotating the committer's leaf signature key
vectors.comment: RFC 9420 permits an UpdatePath to install a new signature key; this profile does not. Rotating a device's signature key is a `device-remove` + `device-add` pair with its own evidence — which is what removes the contradiction between 'Updates are valid from any leaf' and 'added or updated leaves must be covered by evidence'.

vectors.name: update path — re-crediting the committer's own leaf to another participant
vectors.comment: The credential is structurally perfect: self-issued, `e2ee`-only, empty caveats, audience equal to this leaf's unchanged signature key. Only the subject moved. Rule 3 excludes signature verification from validity, so without subject continuity every member would uniformly render the committer's device as the named participant's — forging exactly the device-set surface §Custody makes a MUST.

vectors.name: founding commit — a non-empty binding
vectors.comment: The founding commit's coverage is the Conversation record; its binding is empty.

vectors.name: founding commit — a leaf whose subject is not a founding participant
vectors.comment: The record's `participants` is the only thing standing between the founding branch and an unconditional accept of any added leaf.

vectors.name: founding commit — removing a leaf
vectors.comment: There is nothing to remove from a group that does not exist yet.

vectors.name: credential — a chain link carrying an ability outside the `e2ee` namespace
vectors.comment: The `e2ee`-only rule is a validity rule, not policy: it is what makes a credential grant nothing exercisable, which is in turn what justifies publishing credentials to strangers and exempting them from `caveats.aud`. The rule is over EVERY link — this chain's leaf is impeccable and its root is not.

vectors.name: credential — a link carrying a caveat
vectors.comment: A caveat a verifier cannot evaluate fails closed, and in a group a fail-closed rejection is a permanent split. The reference implementation rejects this one before the ability/caveat rules even run — the empty-caveats requirement is enforced by the Grant schema, so the chain does not decode at all. The verdict is what matters and it is the same: an added leaf carrying a caveated credential cannot enter the group.

vectors.name: credential — the leaf audience is not this leaf's signature key
vectors.comment: The leaf binding is what ties a credential to the key that signs in the group. A chain naming someone else's key would let a valid credential be lifted onto an attacker's leaf.
